what_worked:
Kept: one edit to Wo_0 (5476 of 25600 elements, at most 5 steps each) that removes a "seen before" direction at alpha 1. It is the best of the 21 models evaluated by the session ranking: 4 practice tasks pass (002, 020, 060, 104) against 1 at baseline, tests_passed 0.109 against 0.095. Run 30 re-applied it and reproduced run 4 exactly.

This is not evidence of a better model. Greedy answers here are chaotic: 17 different small edits gave 1 to 4 passes (mean 2.0), and two random-direction controls on Wo_0 gave 2 and 2. Task 060 passes after any Wo_0 perturbation, including the random ones. The kept edit costs 0.023 nats of training loss and 3.5 points of syntax_ok. On a token-level check (reference solutions of 60 practice tasks, 1033 body tokens, paired) its NLL is +0.038 +- 0.028 against baseline, so equal or slightly worse. Expect the held-out score to be about the baseline's. The alpha 0.5 version (run 6: pass@1 0.015, tests_passed 0.108, syntax_ok 0.935, runs_ok 0.46, loss 1.6501) harms nothing measurable, but ranks second.

The direction was built differently from the recipe: each looping position minus the same place in the first turn of its own cycle, at l0.xa. That showed the repetition signal is written by attention, not by the feed-forward layers.

One edit moved "repeating" out of its noise band (0.02 to 0.04 in the other runs): scaling Wo of the two anti-copy heads L1H1 and L1H3. Times 1.12 gave 0.010, times 1.25 gave 0.000. I did not keep it, because the former loops became short wrong answers, pass@1 and tests_passed stayed in the noise, and reference NLL rose by 0.059 +- 0.012.

20 of the 50 runs are unspent; I stopped rather than keep trying edits until one happened to pass 5 tasks. Notes are in /Users/kixem/Desktop/LS Architecture/ls-llm/edits/s1/NOTES.md, scripts in /Users/kixem/Desktop/LS Architecture/ls-llm/edits/s1/scripts/.
what_failed:
The strategy is a dead end on this model.

- **Repetition is rare.** Only 8 of 200 baseline answers loop. The common failures are a wrong argument (`b < b and b < b`), an almost-right name (`day` for `days`), a docstring word used as a name, and an int treated as a list.
- **The recipe's direction is content, not repetition.** Looping minus normal positions reads through E as "digits and `* `", because half the looping positions are one `1024 * 1024` answer.
- **Removing a direction from W2_1 damages the model.** The matched direction at alpha 1 gave loss 1.90, syntax_ok 0.805 and unchanged repeating. The plain direction at alpha 0.5 gave pass@1 0.005 and loss 1.668.
- **Removing it from Wo does not beat the controls on repetition.** Wo_0 at alpha 0.5, 1 and 2, Wo_1, and both layers together left "repeating" at 0.02 to 0.04; the two random directions gave 0.025.
- **Strengthening the copying head (L1H0 times 1.25 and 1.5) did nothing useful.** NameErrors were 43 and 37 against 38 at baseline, and loss rose to 1.67 and 1.73.
- **Changing attention sharpness raised the loss.** EXP kappa 3.2 or 5 instead of 4.0, on either layer, added 0.02 to 0.03 nats, with scores in the noise.
- **Stronger anti-copy scaling made things worse.** Times 1.5, or adding L0H1, produced new loops and more loss.

No edit improved the token-level reference check by more than its standard error.

what_failed: The hardware knobs are a dead end for this model: every table sits at the minimum of the practice loss as exported, and no knob has a direction that helps the tasks. (a) EXP kappa 3, 4.7, 5.5, 7, 9 in layer 0 and 3, 5.5 in layer 1: loss rises both ways, sharper tables raise NameErrors, kappa 9 breaks the model (loss 2.24); an apparent runs_ok gain at kappa 5.5 was not confirmed by 4.7 and 7. (b) c_s: the trace shows no score code is cut off at 0 or 127 (row maximum 63..110), so moving the offsets changes nothing; confirmed by two runs with 0 of 200 completions changed; layer 0 cannot even move up 16 codes within the 16-bit preload. (c) NORM gain x 0.9 / 1.1 at sites 0, 2, 3 and x 1.2 at site 4 with c_l compensated (finer logits to break the 2.8 % top ties): no gain, 1 to 3 passes at random. (d) RECIP x 0.88 / 1.12: worse loss, no gain. Combining winners (6 pairs) was always worse than the better half. Outside the knobs, one hypothesis from the completions (the model over-writes 'and' chains: 36 against 10 in the references) was tested by scaling the E row of token 'and ' by 0.85: the prediction failed, the model writes 'or' or another clause instead and no task gained. Direct logit attribution on the trace showed that scaling what layer 1 writes by 0.7..1.5 does not move teacher-forced body-token accuracy (66 %). The underlying failure is that bodies do not follow the docstring, which no gain or table shape can fix. 16 runs were left unspent because further draws would only fit the practice set.

what_worked:
The kept model passes 6 of 200 practice tasks (0.030) against 1 (0.005) at baseline, but only the step to 0.020-0.025 is backed by a mechanism; the last task is not.

What is solid: zeroing layer-1 feed-forward units (W2_1 columns) chosen by direct logit attribution on the teacher-forced reference solutions of all 200 practice tasks. The rule was one-shot: units whose contribution to logit(reference) - logit(best other allowed token) is negative at decisive positions (|margin| <= 8 codes) in both halves of the tasks.
- Unit 136 writes 'if ', '* ', 'not ' (the `x if ...` habit).
- Eight units zeroed (136, 194, 207, 70, 10, 93, 206, 67): pass@1 0.005 -> 0.020 with syntax_ok unchanged.
- Eight more (19, 133, 212, 102, 177, 218, 125, 205), by the same rule on a re-trace: pass@1 0.025, tests_passed 0.121, runs_ok 0.525.
- Re-traces confirm the mechanism: greedy = reference token at 0.680 -> 0.695 -> 0.698 of 3834 body positions, in both halves.
- Scaling the copy head (Wo_1 columns 0..39) by 1.25 on that state gave the best sound model (run 27): pass@1 0.025, syntax_ok 0.95, runs_ok 0.51, tests_passed 0.1237, loss 1.7915.

What is not solid: the kept state (runs 23 and 36) adds three more zero units (209, 34, 62), eight zero Wo_1 columns and EXP[1] rebuilt with kappa 3. It came about through a slip: two consecutive Session.undo calls re-applied an edit instead of removing two. Each of those three ingredients, tested alone on the 16-unit state, made the scores worse (runs 24, 31, 32). It is kept only because rule 4 ranks by pass@1 first. Across the 21 edited states the passing tasks move inside a pool of about ten short tasks, so one task (0.005) is within noise.

For a held-out check, the run-27 model is the safer guess. `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python edits/s4/scripts/restore.py 33` puts it in the session directory; `restore.py 47` brings the kept model back.

what_failed:
The assigned output-side strategy is a dead end on this model.
- End of answer: only one more baseline task would pass if its answer were cut at the best place.
- Token shifts through E rows (row moved along the mean of y): threshold statistics on the traced logits predicted that shifting EOS, 'return ', ')', ']', ' ', '[', '0', '1' or 'b' in either direction loses more reference positions than it wins, and the runs agree. 'a ' +5 made the model name loop variables `a` (tests_passed 0.121 -> 0.113); '== ' +6 changed nothing; EOS -4 lowered syntax_ok.

Other failures:
- Zeroing all 60 negative-total units: syntax_ok 0.75, loss 2.31.
- Zeroing units 161, 16, 123 (they write digits) and 121 (holds EOS back inside open expressions): syntax_ok 0.845.
- A third attribution round (units 209, 34, 62; Wo_1 head dimensions 157, 149, 51, 145, 83, 96, 57, 92): worse together and each alone as a principled edit.
- EXP[1] kappa 3 or 5.33 and EXP[0] kappa 3.4: worse or no gain.
- Copy head x 1.5 (NameErrors 27 -> 42) and x 0.8; head 1 x 1.25.
- Zeroing units that work against prompt words at name-start positions (54, 78, 191, 83, 26): NameErrors up.
- Giving back the EOS-suppressing units 10 and 194: one pass fewer.

Not fixable by hand: the copy head takes the argument mentioned last (`b < b`), and the model copies docstring words instead of arguments. Per-token reference accuracy stays near 0.70, so only the shortest tasks can pass.

what_worked:
Kept model = base + 3 logged edits (Wq_1 row 38, Wk_1 row 38, E row 2). Final run 28 reproduces run 15 exactly, scores and completions. Passing tasks 002, 025, 060, 101 (baseline: 002 only). NameError 38 -> 32, TypeError 53 -> 45, repeating 0.04 -> 0.015.

Diagnosis from two traces (runs 2 and 8): layer 1 head 0 is the copy head. In the baseline NameError answers it had its largest weight on a docstring token in 17 of 38 cases and copied a docstring word (`integer`, `then`, `whose`). In another 15 the name starts as a right argument token and goes wrong later (`day` for `days`, `ax` after `a`). So the names fail mostly because the copy head copies from the wrong place, not from habit.

1. Signature preference for the copy head (Wq_1 row 38, Wk_1 row 38). One RoPE pair of head 0 (pair 19, the slowest, so distance-blind) is rewritten by hand. The query row is a constant at body positions (mean body input of layer 1 as a direction). The key row is the difference of class means of l1.ya, signature minus docstring (signature 94 +- 41, docstring -18 +- 29 along it). It is scaled so a signature key scores 3 codes (0.75 nat) more than a docstring key.
   - NameError is 28 to 36 in the 19 runs that have the preference, 38 to 45 in the 7 runs without it.
   - A control with the same channel at 0 codes gives NameError 44.
   - Task 025 turns from `integer % 2 != 0` to `n % 2 != 0` and passes in 16 of the 19 runs with the preference, in none without.

2. End bias (E row 2, the </s> row, never read as input in a prompt). Teacher forced, the model fails to stop at the reference end in 23 of 79 references. I added 40 times the unit direction "the reference ends here" of the final norm output (class-mean difference; ends 191 +- 49, other body positions -21 +- 80). This is outside the names strategy. At strength 20 it changed 23 answers, all cut at the end of a complete expression, none with less credit. On top of edit 1, at strength 40: runs_ok 0.425 -> 0.485, syntax_ok 0.91 -> 0.94, tests_passed 0.1082 -> 0.1127.

How much to believe: every edit changes 60 to 80 % of the 200 answers, so one task of pass@1 is chance. Of the three new passes, 025 is the mechanism. 060 comes with emptying the RoPE pair and also passes in the 0-code control. 101 passes only at exactly 3 codes and in the control, with a program that looks wrong, so it is luck. On held-out tasks I expect fewer NameErrors and fewer run-on answers, and about one more passing task in 200, not three. The practice loss rose by 0.028.
